author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Warehouse Flood
challenge.description: A forecast job failed silently for three days, leaving stores ordering blind, and the team never knew until the warehouse was flooded with unsold promotion stock. #reliability_ruth# argues that the performance monitoring must be automated and governed to catch such failures instantly, while #efficiency_emilia# is willing to accept a manual monthly audit of the logs to save on tooling costs.

output.content: I am flagging a hard constraint for the next release cycle. The current workflow has no alerting mechanism to detect when the forecast job fails or degrades. This gap is unacceptable. I will not sign off on any deployment where the monitoring pipeline is absent or broken. We must have automated checks in place that trigger immediate escalation if the nightly batch does not complete successfully. Without this safety net, we are flying blind on system health, which violates our baseline security and reliability standards. This is not a preference or a suggestion for future improvement. It is a mandatory requirement. If the alerting system is not fully operational and verified before we move to production, I will block the release. We cannot expose the supply chain to silent failures again.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they will block the release and refuse to sign off if the alerting mechanism is not present, defining a non-negotiable line whose crossing results in refusal.
